prerequisites: Introduction to differential and integral calculus, linear algebra of vectors and trigonometry.
It is recommended to take the zero-level physics course offered by our university to new engineering students.

learning_outcomes.text: To have knowledge and understanding of the physical principles of mechanics and thermodynamics
To be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve problems in mechanics and thermodynamics using established methods
To be able to design and conduct experiments in mechanics and thermodynamics, to interpret the data obtained, and draw conclusions from them
To have skills in handling laboratory equipment for data collection in mechanics and thermodynamics practicals
To be able to select and use appropriate tools and methods to solve problems in mechanics and thermodynamics
To be able to combine theory and practice to solve problems in mechanics and thermodynamics
Knowledge and understanding of the scientific and mathematical principles underlying their branch of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to solve engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: 1. Kinematics of a particle and relative motion
1.1 Position, velocity, and acceleration vectors. Trajectory equation
2.6 Moment of a force and angular momentum
3. Conservative and non-conservative forces. Work and energy
3.1 Scalar and vector fields. Gradient and curl
3.2 Work and power of a force
4. Dynamics of a system of particles
4.2 Center of mass and center of mass motion
4.3 Kinetic energy of a system of particles
4.4 Conservation theorems for a system of particles
5.2 Rigid body motion in the plane
6.1 Equations of motion of a rigid body: translation and rotation
7.1 Thermodynamics: concepts and definitions. Ideal gas
7.2 Equilibrium states. Quasistatic processes and reversible processes
7.6 Thermal coefficients: thermal expansion and isothermal compressibility
8.1 Heat: heat capacity and specific heat
8.2 Phase transitions: phase diagrams and latent heat
8.3 Internal energy. Internal energy of an ideal gas
8.4 Joule's experiment. First Law of Thermodynamics
8.5 Application of the first law to ideal gases: quasistatic processes
teaching_methods: Problem-solving classes in small groups with direct and active interaction between students and teacher

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (written exams for theoretical concepts)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, attendance at laboratories and submission of practical reports are mandatory. A minimum grade of 3 out of 10 in the final exam is required to pass the course.
